source: It is necessary for students to wear uniforms.
correct: Students have to wear uniforms.
explanation: <Have to> expresa obligación o necesidad externa.

source: It is essential that you arrive on time.
correct: You must arrive on time.
explanation: <Must> expresa obligación fuerte, a menudo impuesta por quien habla.

prompt: Change to past obligation with <had to>
source: We must finish the report by Friday.
correct: We had to finish the report by Friday.
hint: <Must> has no past form — use <had to>
explanation: Obligación en pasado: <had to> reemplaza a <must>, porque <must> no tiene forma de pasado.

source: It isn't necessary for you to come tomorrow.
correct: You don't have to come tomorrow.
explanation: <Don't have to> = no hay obligación, no es necesario.

source: It is prohibited to use phones during the exam.
correct: You mustn't use phones during the exam.
explanation: <Mustn't> = prohibición (no está permitido).

source: You didn't study. That was a mistake.
correct: You should have studied.
explanation: <Should have> + participio pasado expresa un consejo sobre una acción pasada (no ocurrió, pero habría sido lo correcto).

source: It would be a good idea to call her.
correct: You ought to call her.
explanation: <Ought to> da un consejo/recomendación, similar a <should>.

source: She brought an umbrella, but it didn't rain.
correct: She needn't have brought an umbrella.
hint: The action happened but was unnecessary
explanation: <Needn't have> + participio pasado significa que la acción se hizo pero resultó ser innecesaria.

source: Students can leave early on Fridays.
correct: Students are allowed to leave early on Fridays.
explanation: <Be allowed to> es una forma formal/explícita de expresar permiso.

source: I strongly advise you to see a doctor.
correct: You had better see a doctor.
You'd better see a doctor.
hint: <Had better> implies a warning or consequence
explanation: <Had better> da un consejo enfático con una consecuencia negativa implícita si no se sigue.

prompt: Change to past with <wasn't allowed to>
source: Children can't enter this area.
correct: Children weren't allowed to enter that area.
Children were not allowed to enter that area.
explanation: El pasado de <can't> (prohibición) es <wasn't/weren't allowed to>.

source: He had the ability to win, but he didn't try.
correct: He could have won.
He could have won if he had tried.
explanation: <Could have> + participio pasado expresa una habilidad o posibilidad pasada que no se realizó.

source: The rule says employees start at 9 AM.
correct: Employees are supposed to start at 9 AM.
explanation: <Be supposed to> expresa lo que se espera o exige según reglas/acuerdos.

source: I'm sure she is at home. Her car is in the driveway.
correct: She must be at home.
explanation: <Must> + verbo base expresa una deducción lógica fuerte sobre el presente.

source: I'm sure that isn't true.
correct: That can't be true.
explanation: <Can't> + verbo base expresa una deducción negativa (imposible/increíble).

prompt: Rewrite using <must have> for past deduction
source: I'm sure he left early. His desk is empty.
correct: He must have left early.
explanation: <Must have> + participio pasado es una deducción fuerte sobre el pasado.

source: Perhaps she will come to the party.
correct: She might come to the party.
explanation: <Might> expresa posibilidad (menos certeza que <may>).

source: It wasn't necessary to book in advance, so we didn't.
correct: We didn't need to book in advance.
explanation: <Didn't need to> = no era necesario Y la acción no se realizó.

source: He ate the whole cake. Now he feels sick.
correct: He shouldn't have eaten the whole cake.
explanation: <Shouldn't have> + participio pasado expresa crítica sobre una acción pasada.

source: Is it OK if I open the window?
correct: May I open the window?
explanation: <May I...?> es una forma formal de pedir permiso.

source: I prefer to stay at home tonight.
correct: I would rather stay at home tonight.
I'd rather stay at home tonight.
explanation: <Would rather> + verbo base expresa preferencia.

prompt: Rewrite using <can't have> for past deduction
source: I'm sure she didn't say that. She's very polite.
correct: She can't have said that.
explanation: <Can't have> + participio pasado expresa incredulidad sobre un evento pasado.

source: I'm certain he will succeed.
correct: He is bound to succeed.
He's bound to succeed.
explanation: <Be bound to> = estar seguro/con certeza de que algo pasará (predicción fuerte).

prompt: Rewrite using <might have> for past possibility
source: Perhaps she took the wrong bus.
correct: She might have taken the wrong bus.
explanation: <Might have> + participio pasado expresa posibilidad sobre un evento pasado.

source: The meeting was scheduled for 3 PM.
correct: The meeting was to take place at 3 PM.
The meeting was to be at 3 PM.
explanation: <Was/were to> + verbo base expresa un plan o acuerdo formal en el pasado.
